brief.title: Explain NEAR global contracts in 5 bullet points

answer:
- **What it is.** A NEAR *global contract* is program code published once to the network as a whole, rather than stored inside one particular account. Other accounts can point at that shared code instead of each uploading their own copy — like one master recipe kept in a public library instead of every household photocopying it. (NEAR Docs — "Global Contracts": https://docs.near.org/concepts/abstract/global-contracts)

- **The hash is a fingerprint.** Global contract code is identified by its *code hash* — a unique fingerprint computed from the exact bytes of the code. Identical code always yields the identical hash; even a one-character change produces a completely different hash. So approving "this hash" and approving "this exact code" are the same thing. (NEAR Docs — Global Contracts, same page)

- **How an upgrade works.** Someone publishes the new version globally, which creates a new hash. Accounts change behavior only when they deliberately switch to referencing that new hash — nothing moves until the switch, and the code behind the hash can be inspected and tested *before* anyone points to it. (NEAR Docs — Global Contracts, same page)

- **Why that beats a deploy key.** A deploy key is a standing permission: whoever holds it can swap the contract's code at any moment, silently, and everyone finds out afterward — a lost, leaked, or rogue key means arbitrary new code with no notice or vote. Voting on a hash flips this: the upgrade happens only after the group approves that specific fingerprint, and no key exists that could quietly install anything else. The safety shifts from "trust a key holder" to "verify a fingerprint." (Mechanics per NEAR Docs — Global Contracts; the vote-on-hash *procedure* itself is your co-op's governance layer, not something the docs prescribe)

- **Side benefit for members.** Because the code lives once on-chain, storage is cheaper and every account using it runs the identical, reviewed version — one code review covers everyone, rather than many drifting copies. (NEAR Docs — Global Contracts, same page)

**What I could not verify:** I'm working from memory of the NEAR docs and cannot browse, so please confirm the page URL/slug and exact wording on docs.near.org (search "global contracts"). I did not verify specific storage-cost figures, did not cite a numbered NEP, and could not confirm how the docs phrase the deploy-key comparison. The docs also describe referencing global code by account ID (where upgrades follow that account); the hash-referenced form — the immutable one your vote-on-hash process relies on — should be confirmed there too.
